title: ～をください — “Please give me ～”
summary: Noun + をください is the basic way to ask for something: ‘Please give me ～’. It is used in shops, restaurants and when asking people for things. Add a number or counter for quantity.

patterns.gloss: noun + をください (水をください)
noun + を + quantity + ください (切符を二枚ください)

body.p: Say the thing, add を, then ください: 水をください. For amounts, put the number and counter between: 切符を二枚ください (two tickets).
Use it when you want someone to hand you something or to order in a shop: これをください (I'll take this). The を is often dropped in speech: これください.
をください is for asking for a thing. To ask someone to do an action, use verb て-form + ください (書いてください). Adding お in front of the noun (お水をください) makes it even more polite.

examples.ja: 切符（きっぷ）を二枚（にまい）ください。
examples.note: 二枚: number + counter for flat things.

examples.ja: この本（ほん）をください。

pitfalls: Put the quantity before ください: 二枚ください, not ください二枚.
To ask someone to do something, use てください, not をください.
